neighbours.label: the action verb (or 'to') after an urge frame such as 'felt like' or 'want to', usually an impulsive or violent act (throwing, punching, screaming)
fire: The noise got so bad that I felt like smashing the radio against the wall.
Every time he interrupted her, she wanted to slap him across the face.
After losing the final, the coach felt like kicking every chair in the room.
The queue was endless, and I wanted to scream at the top of my lungs.
His smug grin made me feel like hurling my coffee at him.
When the printer jammed again, she felt like ripping it off the desk.
The puppy was so cute that you just want to squeeze it.
Reading the comments made him want to tear his hair out.
quiet: The noise got so bad that I moved the radio into the other room.
Every time he interrupted her, she politely asked him to wait.
After losing the final, the coach calmly reviewed the match footage.
The queue was endless, and I decided to come back the next day.
His smug grin made me roll my eyes and look away.
When the printer jammed again, she opened the tray and removed the paper.
The puppy was so cute that everyone stopped to look at it.
Reading the comments made him close his laptop for the night.
